I brought him to your disciples, but they couldn't do anything for him."

Jesus said, "What a generation! No sense of God! No focus to your lives! How many times do I have to go over these things? How much longer do I have to put up with this? Bring the boy here." He ordered the afflicting demon out — and it was out, gone. From that moment on, the boy was well.
Later, when the disciples had Jesus off to themselves, they asked, "Why couldn't we throw it out?"

"Because you're not yet taking God seriously," Jesus said. "Here's the simple truth: if you had a mere kernel of faith — a poppy seed, say — you could tell this mountain, 'Move!' and it would move. There is nothing you wouldn't be able to tackle."

As they were regrouping in Galilee, Jesus told them, "The Son of Man is about to be betrayed to some people who want nothing to do with God. They will murder him — and three days later he will be raised alive." The disciples were scared to death.
When they arrived at Capernaum, the tax men came to Peter and asked, "Does your teacher pay taxes?"
Peter said, "Of course." But as soon as they were in the house, Jesus confronted him. "Simon, what do you think? When a king levies taxes, who pays — his children or his subjects?"

He answered, "His subjects." Jesus said, "Then the children get off free, right? But so we don't upset them needlessly, go down to the lake, cast a hook, and pull in the first fish that bites. Open its mouth and you'll find a coin. Take it and give it to the tax men. It will be enough for both of us."

title: How to Handle Conflict and Forgive Like a Boss
paragraphs: § Whoever Becomes Simple Again
Around the same time, the disciples came to Jesus asking, "Who gets the highest rank in God's kingdom?"

For an answer, Jesus called a little kid over and stood him right in the middle of the room. "I'm telling you, once and for all: unless you return to square one and start over like children, you're not even going to get a look at the kingdom, let alone get in. Whoever becomes simple and elemental again, like this child, will rank high in God's kingdom. And here's more: when you welcome the childlike because of me, it's the same as welcoming me."

"But if you give these little ones a hard time — bullying them or taking advantage of their simple trust — you'll soon wish you hadn't. You'd be better off dropped in the middle of the lake with a millstone around your neck. Doom to the world for giving these God-believing kids a hard time! Hard times are inevitable, but you don't have to make it worse — and it's doomsday for you if you do."

"If your hand or your foot gets in the way of God, chop it off and throw it away. You're better off maimed or lame and alive than owning two hands and two feet and ending up godless in a furnace of eternal fire. And if your eye distracts you from God, pull it out and throw it away. You're better off one-eyed and alive than seeing perfectly from inside the fire of hell."
"Watch that you don't look down on a single one of these childlike believers. You realize, don't you, that their personal angels are constantly in touch with my Father in heaven?"
§ Work It Out Between You

"Look at it this way: if someone has a hundred sheep and one of them wanders off, doesn't he leave the ninety-nine and go after the one? And if he finds it, isn't he way more thrilled over that one than over the ninety-nine that stayed put? Your Father in heaven feels the same way — he doesn't want to lose even one of these simple believers."

"If a fellow believer hurts you, go and tell him — work it out between the two of you. If he listens, you've made a friend. If he won't listen, take one or two others along so the witnesses keep things honest, and try again. If he still won't listen, tell the church. And if he won't listen to the church either, you'll have to start over from scratch — confront him with the need to turn around, and offer him God's forgiving love again."

"Take this most seriously: a yes on earth is a yes in heaven; a no on earth is a no in heaven. What you say to one another is eternal — I mean this. When two of you get together on anything at all on earth and make a prayer of it, my Father in heaven goes into action. And when two or three of you are together because of me, you can be sure that I'll be there."
At that point Peter got up the nerve to ask, "Master, how many times do I forgive a brother or sister who hurts me? Seven?"
Jesus replied, "Seven! Hardly. Try seventy times seven. Stop keeping score."
§ A Story About Forgiveness

"God's kingdom is like a king who decided to square accounts with his servants. As he got under way, they brought him a servant who had run up a debt of a hundred thousand dollars. He couldn't pay up, so the king ordered the man — along with his wife, children, and goods — to be auctioned off at the slave market."
"The poor wretch threw himself at the king's feet and begged, 'Give me a chance and I'll pay it all back.' Touched by his plea, the king let him off — erasing the debt."
"The servant was no sooner out of the room when he came upon one of his fellow servants who owed him ten dollars. He seized him by the throat and demanded, 'Pay up. Now!'"

"The poor wretch threw himself down and begged, 'Give me a chance and I'll pay it all back.' But he wouldn't do it — he had him arrested and put in jail until the debt was paid. When the other servants saw this going on, they were outraged and brought a detailed report to the king."

"The king summoned the man and said, 'You evil servant! I forgave your entire debt when you begged me for mercy. Shouldn't you be compelled to be merciful to your fellow servant who asked for mercy?' The king was furious and put the screws to the man until he paid back his entire debt. And that's exactly what my Father in heaven is going to do to each one of you who doesn't forgive — unconditionally — anyone who asks for mercy."

title: The Rich Young Ruler
paragraphs: Jesus finished up all his teaching, then packed his bags and left Galilee. He crossed over into the region of Judea, on the other side of the Jordan River. Huge crowds totally swarmed him there, and he healed everyone who needed it.
§ Divorce

One day, the Pharisees (a religious group known for being super strict) started bugging him, trying to trap him. They asked, "Is it even allowed for a guy to divorce his wife for just any random reason?"

Jesus shot back, "Seriously, haven't you guys read in your Bibles? Right from the start, the Creator made humans as male and female, specifically for each other. That's why a guy leaves his dad and mom, sticks super close to his wife, and they become 'one flesh' – not two separate people anymore, but one united being. Since God himself designed this deep, organic connection between a man and a woman, nobody should mess with his masterpiece by tearing them apart."
They immediately hit back, "Okay, if that's the deal, then why did Moses (the ancient prophet) give instructions about getting divorce papers and how to go about it?"

Jesus explained, "Moses allowed for divorce because your hearts were so stubborn and hard. But that was never God's original intention or part of his perfect plan. I'm holding you to that original plan: if you divorce your faithful wife and then marry someone else, you're responsible for adultery (being unfaithful). The only exception I make is if your spouse has already cheated on you."
Jesus' disciples were like, "Whoa, if those are the rules for marriage, then we don't stand a chance! Why even bother getting married?"

But Jesus replied, "Look, not everyone is mature enough or wired to live a married life. It takes a certain knack and a lot of grace. Marriage isn't for everyone, for real. Some people, right from birth, just don't seem to think about marriage. Others never get asked – or accepted – for marriage. And some decide not to get married because of what they want to do for God's kingdom. But if you're capable of growing into the awesome bigness of marriage, then go for it!"
§ To Enter God’s Kingdom

Another day, some parents brought their kids to Jesus, hoping he'd lay his hands on them and pray over them. But the disciples tried to shoo them away. Jesus stepped in though, saying, "Leave the children alone! Don't stop them from coming to me. God's kingdom is made up of people just like these little ones."
After he laid his hands on them, he moved on.
Then, a guy came up to Jesus and asked, "Teacher, what good thing do I need to do to get eternal life?"
Jesus responded, "Why are you asking me about what's good? Only God is truly good. If you want to jump into the life God offers, just do what he tells you."
The man asked, "What specifically?"
Jesus listed them out: "Don't murder, don't commit adultery, don't steal, don't lie, honor your father and mother, and love your neighbor as much as you love yourself."
The young man said, "I've done all that stuff since I was little! What else is there?"

"If you want to go all-in," Jesus replied, "go sell everything you own; give all that money to the poor. Then you'll have all your real treasure waiting for you in heaven. After that, come follow me."

That was totally the last thing the young man expected to hear. He walked away looking super bummed out, crestfallen. He was holding on tight to a lot of stuff, and he just couldn't bring himself to let go.

As he watched him leave, Jesus told his disciples, "Do you guys have any idea how hard it is for rich people to get into God's kingdom? Let me tell you, it's easier to squeeze a camel through the eye of a needle than for someone rich to get into God's kingdom."
The disciples were completely shocked. "Then who even has a chance at all?!"
Jesus looked them straight in the eye and said, "You have no chance at all if you think you can pull it off on your own. But you have every chance in the world if you trust God to do it."
Then Peter jumped in, "Hey, we left everything and followed you! What do we get out of it?"

Jesus replied, "Yes, you have followed me. In the re-creation of the world, when the Son of Man (Jesus himself) will rule gloriously, you who have followed me will also rule, starting with the twelve tribes of Israel. And it's not just you guys, but anyone who gives up their home, family, land – whatever – because of me will get it all back a hundred times over, plus the huge bonus of eternal life. This is the Great Reversal: a lot of people who are first now will end up last, and the last will end up first."

title: The Unfair Paycheck and Upside-Down Leadership
paragraphs: Jesus told a story to explain how God's grace works: A farm owner went out at 6:00 AM to hire day laborers to work in his vineyard. They agreed on a standard full-day's wage. At 9:00 AM, the owner saw more guys standing around unemployed, so he hired them too. He did the same thing at noon, at 3:00 PM, and again at 5:00 PM, when he found more guys still just standing around. He asked them, 'Why are you standing around doing nothing all day?' They said, 'Because no one hired us.' So he told them, 'Go work in my vineyard too.'

When it was time to get paid, the boss told his manager to pay the guys hired at 5:00 PM first. He gave them a full day's wage. When the guys who had been sweating in the sun since 6:00 AM stepped up, they expected a massive bonus. But the boss gave them the exact same full-day's wage they had agreed on. The early crew was furious. "This is completely unfair! We worked twelve hours in the blistering heat, and you paid those lazy guys the same amount!" The boss replied, "Friend, I didn't cheat you. We agreed on a price, and I paid it. Take your money and go. I decided to give the one who came last the same as you. Can't I be generous with my own money? Are you jealous because I'm kind?" Jesus summed it up: "The last will be first, and the first will be last."

Then Jesus pulled the Twelve aside on the road and said, 'Listen to me carefully. We're heading up to Jerusalem. When we get there, the Son of Man is going to be betrayed to the religious leaders and scholars. They'll sentence him to death, then hand him over to the Romans, who will mock him, torture him, and crucify him. But on the third day, he will be raised up alive.'

A Mom's Ambitious Request As they got closer to Jerusalem, the mother of James and John, Zebedee's sons (two of the disciples), came up to Jesus and kneeled down with a request. "What do you want?" Jesus asked. She said, "When you become King, promise me that my two boys can be your right-hand and left-hand men." Jesus looked at the brothers. "You have no idea what you're asking. Can you drink from the cup of suffering I'm about to drink from?" They confidently said, "We can handle it." Jesus said, "You will suffer like me, but I don't assign the honored seats. My Father does."
When the other ten disciples heard about this, they lost their tempers, thoroughly disgusted with James and John. Jesus called a team meeting to shut it down:

"You guys know how godless rulers do leadership—they throw their weight around, a little power goes straight to their heads, and they make everyone serve them. It is not going to be like that with you. Whoever wants to be a leader among you must be your servant. Whoever wants to be first must be your slave. I, the Son of Man, didn't come here to be served by you. I came to serve you, and to give my life to buy freedom for many."

As they were leaving Jericho, a huge crowd followed. Two blind men were sitting by the side of the road, and when they heard Jesus was passing by, they shouted, "Master, Son of David, have mercy on us!" The crowd told them to shut up, but they yelled even louder. Jesus stopped and asked, "What do you want Me to do for you?" They said, "Master, we want to see!" Jesus was deeply moved, touched their eyes — and instantly they could see. They got up and joined the crowd following Him.

title: Jesus Makes A Scene
paragraphs: As Jesus and his crew got close to Jerusalem and arrived at Bethphage on the Mount of Olives, he sent two disciples on a mission. 'Go over to the village across from you,' he said, 'and you'll find a donkey tethered there, her colt with her. Untie them and bring them to me. If anyone gives you a hard time, just say, ‘The Master needs them,’ and they’ll let you go.' This was the prophet's words coming true: 'Tell Zion's daughter: Look, your king is on his way, humble and ready, riding on a donkey — on a colt, the foal of a pack animal.' So the disciples did exactly what Jesus told them to do. They led the donkey and colt out, laid some of their clothes on them, and Jesus hopped on. The crowd went absolutely wild, throwing their jackets on the road like a red carpet and cutting branches from the trees to throw down like a welcome mat. Crowds went ahead and crowds followed, all of them screaming, 'Hosanna to David's son! Blessed is he who comes in God's name! Hosanna in the highest heaven!'

The whole city was buzzing, like, 'What's going on here? Who IS this guy?' The crowd with Jesus was shouting, 'This is Jesus, the prophet — the one from Nazareth in Galilee!' Then Jesus went straight to the Temple and lost it. He threw out everyone who had set up shop there, buying and selling. He started flipping tables of the loan sharks and kicking over the stalls of people selling pigeons. He went beast mode, quoting the scriptures: My house was designated a house of prayer; You have made it a hangout for thieves. After he cleared them out, the blind and the crippled came to him and he healed them right there.

The religious leaders were fuming when they saw all the incredible things he was doing. But what really set them off were the kids running around the Temple shouting, 'Hosanna to the Son of David!' They confronted Jesus, all heated. 'Do you hear what these kids are saying?' Jesus just looked at them and said, 'Yeah, I hear them. Haven't you ever read the scripture that says, ‘From the mouths of children and babies I’ll furnish a place of praise’?'. Mic drop. He was so over their drama that he just turned and walked out of the city to spend the night in Bethany.

The next morning, Jesus was walking back to the city and feeling hungry. He saw a fig tree by the road and went to get some breakfast, but it only had leaves. So he said to the tree, 'No more figs from you—ever!' And right then, the tree withered up into a dry stick. His disciples saw it and their jaws dropped. 'How did that tree just die on the spot?' they asked. Jesus told them, 'Seriously, if you embrace this kingdom life and don’t doubt God, you can do way more than what I just did to the fig tree. You could tell this mountain, ‘Go jump in the lake,’ and it would. If you believe, you will receive whatever you ask for in prayer.'

Back in the Temple, the high priests and elders cornered him while he was teaching. 'Show us your credentials,' they demanded. 'Who gave you the authority to do all this?' Jesus shot back, 'I'll answer you, but first, you answer me. John the Baptist’s baptism—was it from heaven or from humans?' They were totally stuck. They huddled up, whispering, 'If we say ‘from heaven,’ he’ll ask why we didn’t believe John. If we say ‘from humans,’ the crowd will riot because they all think John was a prophet.' So they came back and said, 'We don’t know.' Jesus replied, 'Then I’m not telling you who gave me my authority either.'

Then Jesus dropped a story on them. 'Tell me what you think of this: A man had two sons. He went up to the first and said, ‘Son, go out for the day and work in the vineyard.’ The son said, ‘I don’t want to,’ but later he changed his mind and went. The father told the second son the same thing, and he said, ‘Yes, sir!’ but he never went. Which one did what the father wanted?' They answered, 'The first one.' Jesus looked them dead in the eye and said, 'Well, I’m telling you, the tax collectors and immoral women are getting into God’s kingdom ahead of you. John the Baptist came and showed you the right way to live, and you dissed him, but they believed him. Even after seeing their lives change, you still didn’t change your minds and believe.'

He wasn't done yet. 'Listen to this. A landowner planted a vineyard — fenced it, dug a winepress, put up a watchtower — and rented it to some farmers before going off on a trip. When it was harvest time, he sent his servants to collect his share. But the farmers grabbed the first servant and beat him up, killed another, and stoned a third — but that one got away. He sent more servants, and they got the same treatment. The owner was at the end of his rope. Finally, he sent his son, thinking, ‘Surely they’ll respect my son.’ But when the farmers saw the son arrive, they rubbed their hands in greed and said, ‘This is the heir! Let’s kill him and take his inheritance!' So they grabbed him, threw him out of the vineyard, and murdered him.'

Jesus paused and asked the leaders, 'So when the owner of the vineyard comes back, what will he do to those farmers?' They replied, 'He’ll bring those wretches to a wretched end, and he’ll rent the vineyard to other farmers who will give him his share at harvest time.' Jesus said, 'Exactly. And you've read the scripture: The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. This is the Lord’s doing, and it is marvelous in our eyes. Therefore I tell you that the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a people who will produce its fruit. Trip over this Stone and you'll get shattered; let it fall on you and you'll get crushed.' When the religious leaders heard his stories, they knew he was talking about them. They wanted to arrest him, but they were scared of the crowd, who all thought Jesus was a prophet.

title: Party Crashers & Gotcha Questions
paragraphs: § The Story of the Wedding Banquet

Jesus dropped another parable on them. He said, "God's kingdom is like a king who threw a wedding banquet for his son. He sent out servants to call in all the invited guests — and they wouldn't come!"

He sent out another round of servants with the message: 'Look, everything is on the table, the prime rib is ready for carving. Come to the feast!' But the guests couldn't be bothered. One went off to weed his garden, another to work in his shop. The rest, with nothing better to do, beat up the messengers — and then killed them. The king was outraged. He sent his soldiers to destroy those thugs and level their city.

Then he told his servants, 'We have a wedding banquet all prepared but no guests. The ones I invited weren't up to it. Go out into the busiest intersections in town and invite anyone you find to the banquet.' The servants went out on the streets and rounded up everyone they laid eyes on, good and bad, regardless — and the wedding hall was packed. But when the king entered and looked over the scene, he spotted a man who wasn't properly dressed. 'Friend,' he said, 'how dare you come in here looking like that!' The man was speechless. Then the king told his servants, 'Get him out of here — fast. Tie him up and ship him to hell, and make sure he doesn't get back in.' That's what Jesus meant when he said, 'Many get invited; only a few make it.'
§ Paying Taxes

That's when the Pharisees plotted a way to trap him into saying something damaging. They sent their disciples, with a few of Herod's followers mixed in, to ask, 'Teacher, we know you've got integrity — you teach God's way accurately, you don't care about popular opinion, and you don't play favorites with your students. So tell us straight: is it right to pay taxes to Caesar or not?' Jesus knew they were up to no good. 'Why are you playing these games with me? Why are you trying to trap me? Got a coin? Let me see it.' They handed him a silver coin.

'This engraving — who does it look like? And whose name is on it?' 'Caesar's,' they said. 'Then give Caesar what is his, and give God what is his.' The Pharisees were speechless. They went off shaking their heads.
§ Marriage and Resurrection

That same day, some Sadducees — the party that says there's no such thing as resurrection — came at him with a wild hypothetical. 'Teacher, Moses said that if a man dies childless, his brother is obligated to marry the widow and father a child with her. So here's a case: there were seven brothers. The first brother married her and died with no kids, so his wife passed to his brother. The second brother also left her childless, then the third — on and on, all seven. Finally the wife died. Now here's our question: at the resurrection, whose wife is she? She was a wife to each of them.'

Jesus answered, 'You're off base on two counts: you don't know what God said, and you don't know how God works. At the resurrection we're beyond marriage. Like the angels, all our ecstasies and intimacies then will be with God. And regarding your little theory about whether the dead are raised — don't you read your Bibles? The grammar is clear: God says, 'I am — not *was* — the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, the God of Jacob.' The living God defines himself not as the God of dead men, but of the *living*.' Hearing this exchange, the crowd was seriously impressed.
§ The Most Important Command

When the Pharisees heard how he had bested the Sadducees, they gathered their forces for another assault. One of their religion scholars spoke for them, posing a question they hoped would show him up: 'Teacher, which command in God's Law is the most important?' Jesus said, ''Love the Lord your God with all your passion and prayer and intelligence.' This is the most important, the first on any list. But there's a second to set alongside it: 'Love others as well as you love yourself.' These two commands are pegs — everything in God's Law and the Prophets hangs from them.'
§ David's Son and Master

As the Pharisees were regrouping, Jesus caught them off balance with his own test question: 'What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is he?' 'David's son,' they said. Jesus replied, 'Well, if the Christ is David's son, how do you explain that David, under inspiration, named Christ his 'Master'? God said to my Master, 'Sit here at my right hand until I make your enemies your footstool.' Now if David calls him 'Master,' how can he at the same time be his son?' That stumped them, literalists that they were. Unwilling to risk losing face again in one of these public verbal exchanges, they quit asking questions for good.

title: Jesus Calls Out on the Hypocrites
paragraphs: § Religious Fashion Shows

Jesus turned to address his disciples, along with the crowd that had gathered with them. 'The religion scholars and Pharisees are competent teachers in God's Law — you won't go wrong following their teachings on Moses. But be careful about following *them*. They talk a good line, but they don't live it. They don't take it into their hearts and live it out in their behavior. It's all spit-and-polish veneer. Instead of giving you God's Law as food and drink by which you can banquet on God, they package it in bundles of rules, loading you down like pack animals. They seem to take pleasure in watching you stagger under these loads, and wouldn't think of lifting a finger to help. Their lives are perpetual fashion shows — embroidered prayer shawls one day and flowery prayers the next. They love to sit at the head table at church dinners, basking in the most prominent positions, preening in the radiance of public flattery, receiving honorary degrees, and getting called 'Doctor' and 'Reverend.'

Then Jesus flipped the script. 'Don't let people do that to *you* — put you on a pedestal like that. You all have a single Teacher, and you are all classmates. Don't set people up as experts over your life, letting them tell you what to do. Save that authority for God; let *him* tell you what to do. No one else should carry the title of 'Father'; you have only one Father, and he's in heaven. And don't let people maneuver you into taking charge of them. There is only one Life-Leader for you and them — Christ. Do you want to stand out? Then step down. Be a servant. If you puff yourself up, you'll get the wind knocked out of you. But if you're content to simply be yourself, your life will count for plenty.'
§ Frauds!
'I've had it with you! You're hopeless, you religion scholars, you Pharisees! Frauds! Your lives are roadblocks to God's kingdom. You refuse to enter, and won't let anyone else in either!'
'You're hopeless, you religion scholars and Pharisees! Frauds! You go halfway around the world to make a convert, but once you get him you make him into a replica of yourselves, double-damned!'

'You're hopeless! What arrogant stupidity! You say, 'If someone makes a promise with his fingers crossed, that's nothing; but if he swears with his hand on the Bible, that's serious.' What ignorance! Does the leather on the Bible carry more weight than the skin on your hands? And what about this piece of trivia: 'If you shake hands on a promise, that's nothing; but if you raise your hand that God is your witness, that's serious'? What ridiculous hairsplitting! What difference does it make whether you shake hands or raise hands? A promise is a promise. What difference does it make if you make your promise inside or outside a house of worship? A promise is a promise. God is present, watching and holding you to account regardless.'

'You're hopeless, you religion scholars and Pharisees! Frauds! You keep meticulous account books, tithing on every nickel and dime you get, but on the meat of God's Law, things like fairness and compassion and commitment — the absolute basics! — you carelessly take it or leave it. Careful bookkeeping is commendable, but the basics are required. Do you have any idea how silly you look, writing a life story that's wrong from start to finish, nitpicking over commas and semicolons?'

'You're hopeless, you religion scholars and Pharisees! Frauds! You buff the surface of your cups and bowls so they sparkle in the sun, while the insides are maggoty with your greed and gluttony. Stupid Pharisee! Scour the insides, and then the gleaming surface will mean something.'

'You're hopeless, you religion scholars and Pharisees! Frauds! You're like manicured grave plots, grass clipped and the flowers bright, but six feet down it's all rotting bones and worm-eaten flesh. People look at you and think you're saints, but beneath the skin you're total frauds.'

'You're hopeless, you religion scholars and Pharisees! Frauds! You build granite tombs for your prophets and marble monuments for your saints. And you say that if you had lived in the days of your ancestors, no blood would have been on your hands. You protest too much! You're cut from the same cloth as those murderers, and daily add to the death count.'

'Snakes! Cold-blooded sneaks! Do you think you can worm your way out of this? Never have to pay the piper? It's on account of people like you that I send prophets and wise guides and scholars generation after generation — and generation after generation you treat them like dirt, greeting them with lynch mobs, hounding them with abuse. You can't squirm out of this: Every drop of righteous blood ever spilled on this earth, beginning with the blood of that good man Abel right down to the blood of Zechariah, Barachiah's son, whom you murdered at his prayers, is on your head. All this, I'm telling you, is coming down on you, on your generation.'

'Jerusalem! Jerusalem! Murderer of prophets! Killer of the ones who brought you God's news! How often I've ached to embrace your children, the way a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you wouldn't let me. And now you're so desolate, nothing but a ghost town. What is there left to say? Only this: I'm out of here soon. The next time you see me you'll say, 'Oh, God has blessed him! He's come, bringing God's rule!''

title: The Real Tea on the End Times
paragraphs: § Routine History

As Jesus and his crew were leaving the Temple, his disciples were totally geeking out over the amazing architecture. 'Hey, Jesus, check out these buildings! So epic!' Jesus just shook his head. 'You're not impressed by all this sheer *size*, are you? The truth of the matter is that there's not a stone in that building that is not going to end up in a pile of rubble.' Later, they were chilling on the Mount of Olives, and the disciples cornered him. 'Okay, spill. When is all this going down? What's going to be the sign of your coming — that the time's up?'

Jesus got real serious. 'Watch out for doomsday deceivers. A bunch of fakes are going to show up with forged identities, claiming 'I am Christ, the Messiah' — and they're going to deceive a lot of people. You'll hear about wars, and rumors of more wars, but keep your head and don't panic. This is routine history; this is no sign of the end. Nation will fight nation and ruler fight ruler, over and over. Famines and earthquakes will hit various places. This is nothing compared to what's coming.'

'Then things get personal. They're going to throw you to the wolves and kill you — everyone will hate you because you carry my name. And then, going from bad to worse, it will be dog-eat-dog, everyone at each other's throat, everyone hating each other. In the confusion, lying preachers will come forward and deceive a lot of people. For many others, the overwhelming spread of evil will do them in — nothing left of their love but a mound of ashes. But staying with it — that's what God requires. Stay with it to the end. You won't be sorry, and you'll be saved. All during this time, the good news — the Message of the kingdom — will be preached all over the world, a witness staked out in every country. And then the end will come.'
§ The Monster of Desecration

'But be ready to run for it when you see the monster of desecration set up in the Temple sanctuary. The prophet Daniel described this. If you've read Daniel, you'll know what I'm talking about. If you're living in Judea at the time, run for the hills. If you're working in the yard, don't return to the house to get anything. If you're out in the field, don't go back and get your coat. Pregnant and nursing mothers will have it especially hard. Hope and pray this won't happen during the winter or on a Sabbath. This is going to be trouble on a scale beyond what the world has ever seen, or will see again. If these days of trouble were left to run their course, nobody would make it. But on account of God's chosen people, the trouble will be cut short.'
§ The Arrival of the Son of Man

'If anyone tries to flag you down, calling out, 'Here's the Messiah!' or points, 'There he is!' — don't fall for it. Fake Messiahs and lying preachers are going to pop up everywhere. Their impressive credentials and bewitching performances will pull the wool over the eyes of even those who ought to know better. But I've given you fair warning. So if they say, 'Run to the country and see him arrive!' or, 'Quick, get downtown, see him come!' — don't give them the time of day. The Arrival of the Son of Man isn't something you go to see. He comes like swift lightning — to you! Whenever you see crowds gathering, think of carrion vultures circling, moving in, hovering over a rotting carcass. You can be quite sure that it's not the living Son of Man pulling in those crowds.'

'Following those hard times, Sun will fade out, moon cloud over, Stars fall out of the sky, cosmic powers tremble. Then, the Arrival of the Son of Man! It will fill the skies — no one will miss it. Unready people all over the world, outsiders to the splendor and power, will raise a huge lament as they watch the Son of Man blazing out of heaven. At that same moment, he'll dispatch his angels with a trumpet-blast summons, pulling in God's chosen from the four winds, from pole to pole.'

'Take a lesson from the fig tree. From the moment you notice its buds form, the merest hint of green, you know summer's just around the corner. So it is with you: When you see all these things, you'll know he's at the door. Don't take this lightly. I'm not just saying this for some future generation, but for all of you. This age continues until all these things take place. Sky and earth will wear out; my words won't wear out.'

'But the exact day and hour? No one knows that, not even heaven's angels, not even the Son. Only the Father knows. The Arrival of the Son of Man will take place in times like Noah's. Before the great flood everyone was carrying on as usual, having a good time right up to the day Noah boarded the ark. They knew nothing — until the flood hit and swept everything away. The Son of Man's Arrival will be like that: Two men will be working in the field — one will be taken, one left behind; two women will be grinding at the mill — one will be taken, one left behind. So stay awake, alert. You have no idea what day your Master will show up. But you do know this: You know that if the homeowner had known what time of night the burglar would arrive, he would have been there with his dogs to prevent the break-in. Be vigilant just like that. You have no idea when the Son of Man is going to show up.'

'Who here qualifies for the job of overseeing the kitchen? A person the Master can depend on to feed the workers on time each day. Someone the Master can drop in on unannounced and always find him doing his job. A God-blessed man or woman, I tell you. It won't be long before the Master will put this person in charge of the whole operation. But if that person only looks out for himself, and the minute the Master is away does what he pleases — abusing the help and throwing drunken parties for his friends — the Master is going to show up when he least expects it, and it won't be pretty. He'll end up in the dump with the hypocrites, out in the cold shivering, teeth chattering.'

title: Stay Ready or Get Left Behind
paragraphs: Jesus dropped another parable. He said, 'God's Kingdom is like ten bridesmaids waiting for the groom to show up for the wedding party. Five of them were totally clueless and the other five were on top of their game. The clueless ones brought their lamps but forgot to bring extra oil, like showing up to a journey with no extra supplies. The smart ones? They brought a whole backup supply.

The groom was running late, so all the girls ended up crashing for a nap. Then, in the middle of the night, someone screamed, 'He's here! The groom is finally here! Let's go!' All ten of them jumped up and got their lamps ready. But the five unprepared girls started to panic. 'Our lamps are dying! Quick, give us some of your oil!'

The smart girls said, 'Sorry, no can do. There isn't enough for all of us. You'll have to run to the store and buy your own.' So they left to go buy more, but while they were gone, the groom arrived. The girls who were ready went into the wedding feast with him, and the door was locked. A little while later, the clueless crew finally showed up, banging on the door. 'Master, let us in!' But he just said, 'Do I even know you? I don't think so.' Then Jesus looked at his crew and said, 'So for real, stay alert. You have no idea when the time will come.'

Then Jesus hit them with another story. 'It's like a boss who was going on a long trip. He called in his top three employees and gave them some major cash to manage. To one, he gave $5,000, to another $2,000, and to the last one $1,000—all based on what he knew they could handle. The first guy immediately went out and hustled, doubling the investment. The second guy did the same. But the third guy, the one with the $1,000, just dug a hole and buried it. He played it way too safe.'

After a super long time, the boss came back to see what was up. The guy with the $5,000 showed him the $10,000 he made. The boss was thrilled! 'Let's go! You killed it! You're not just my employee anymore, you're my partner.' The guy with the $2,000 showed him his $4,000, and the boss said the exact same thing. But then the third guy came up and said, 'Look, I know you're a tough boss and you don't mess around. I was scared I'd mess up and lose your money, so I just hid it. Here's your $1,000 back, safe and sound.'

The boss absolutely lost it. 'You're a terrible employee! It's criminal to be that cautious! If you knew I was serious about results, why did you do the absolute least? You could have at least put it in a savings account and gotten some interest!' Then he told his other guys, 'Take his $1,000 and give it to the one who made the most. And throw this play-it-safe guy out. He's getting kicked out of the company for good.'

Jesus wasn't done. He dropped a bomb. 'When the Son of Man comes back in all his glory with his angel squad, he's going to sit on his throne and judge everyone. All the nations will be lined up, and he'll separate people like a farmer separates sheep from goats. The sheep will be on his right, and the goats on his left.'

Then the King will turn to the sheep on his right and say, 'Come on in, you're blessed by my Father! Your spot in the kingdom has been ready since day one. Why? Because when I was hungry, you fed me. When I was thirsty, you gave me a drink. When I was a stranger, you took me in. When I was freezing, you gave me clothes. When I was sick, you checked on me. When I was in jail, you visited me.'

The sheep will be totally confused. 'Wait, what? When did we ever see you hungry or thirsty or sick or in jail?' And the King will say, 'I'm telling you the honest truth: whenever you did one of these things for the least important person, you were doing it for me.'

Then he'll turn to the goats on his left and go beast mode. 'Get out of here, you useless goats! You're headed for eternal fire. Why? Because I was hungry, and you didn't give me any food. I was thirsty, and you gave me nothing to drink. I was a stranger, and you ignored me. I was freezing, and you didn't offer a coat. I was sick and in jail, and you never even thought to visit.' They'll argue back, 'Master, when did we ever see you hungry or thirsty or homeless or shivering or sick or in prison and not help?' And he'll reply, 'Seriously, whenever you failed to help someone who was overlooked, you were failing to help me.' And those goats will be sent to their eternal punishment, but the sheep will enter eternal life.

title: The Final Hours
paragraphs: Jesus dropped a bomb on his disciples, saying, 'You know Passover is in two days? That's when the Son of Man gets betrayed and crucified.' At that very moment, the high priests and religious leaders were meeting at the house of Caiaphas the high priest, conspiring to grab Jesus by stealth and kill him. They agreed not to do it during the festival, though — 'We don't want a riot on our hands.'

While Jesus was having dinner at Simon the Leper's house, a woman came in and did something totally extra. She poured a whole bottle of super expensive perfume on him. The disciples lost it, saying, 'What a waste! That could have been sold and the money given to the poor!' But Jesus shut them down, saying, 'Why are you giving her a hard time? She did a beautiful thing for me. You'll always have the poor with you, but you won't always have me. She was preparing me for my burial. I promise you, wherever the good news is preached, what she has done will be told in memory of her.'

That's when Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went full-on snake. He went to the chief priests and asked, 'What will you give me if I hand him over to you?' They offered him thirty pieces of silver, and from then on, he was looking for the right moment to betray Jesus.

On the first day of the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the disciples asked Jesus, 'Where do you want us to get the Passover meal ready?' Jesus said, 'Head into the city and find a certain guy. Tell him, "The Teacher says: My time is almost here — me and my disciples are celebrating Passover at your place."' The disciples followed his instructions to the letter and got the meal ready. That evening, Jesus sat down at the table with the Twelve, and right in the middle of dinner he dropped something heavy on them: 'I have something hard but important to tell you — one of you is going to hand me over to the conspirators.' They were stunned, and one by one they started asking, 'It isn't me, is it, Master?' Jesus answered, 'It's someone I eat with every day — someone who passes me food right here at this table. In one sense, the Son of Man is walking straight into the betrayal the Scriptures already mapped out — no surprises here. But in another sense, the guy who turns traitor on the Son of Man? It would have been better for him if he'd never been born.' Then Judas, already turned traitor, said, 'It isn't me, is it, Rabbi?' Jesus said, 'Don't play games with me, Judas.'

During the meal, Jesus took some bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to his disciples. 'Take, eat. This is my body.' Then he took a cup of wine, thanked God for it, and said, 'Drink this, all of you. This is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.'

"I'm telling you, I won't drink wine again until the day I drink it with you in My Father's kingdom." Then they sang a hymn and headed out to the Mount of Olives. On the way, Jesus told them, "Tonight, every one of you is going to bail on Me. There's a Scripture that says, \"I'll strike the shepherd, and the sheep will scatter.\" But after I'm raised back to life, I'll go ahead of you to Galilee." Peter shot back, "Even if everyone else bails, I never will!" Jesus said, "I'm telling you the truth — tonight, before the rooster crows, you're going to deny Me three times." Peter insisted, "Even if I have to die with You, I'll never deny You!" And all the other disciples said the exact same thing.

Then Jesus took them to a garden called Gethsemane. 'Stay here while I go over there to pray,' he told the disciples. He took Peter and the two sons of Zebedee with him, and he plunged into the heaviest sorrow imaginable. 'This sorrow is crushing the life out of me,' he said. 'Stay here and keep watch with me.' He went a little further ahead, fell face-down on the ground, and prayed, 'My Father, if there's any way, get me out of this. But please — not what I want. You — what do you want?' When he came back, he found them sound asleep. He said to Peter, 'Seriously? You can't stick it out with me for a single hour? Stay alert and pray, so you don't wander into temptation without even knowing you're in danger. Part of you is totally eager, ready for anything in God — but the other part is as lazy as an old dog sleeping by the fire.' He left them and went to pray a second time: 'My Father, if there's no other way but drinking this cup down to the last drop, I'm ready. Do it your way.' When he came back, they were asleep again — they just couldn't keep their eyes open. This time he let them sleep and went back a third time to pray, going over the same ground one last time. Then he came back and said, 'Are you really going to sleep on and make a night of it? My time is up — the Son of Man is about to be handed over to sinners. Get up! Let's go! Here comes my betrayer.'

The words were barely out of his mouth when Judas — one of the Twelve — showed up with a gang sent by the high priests and religious leaders, all armed with swords and clubs. The betrayer had worked out a signal with them: 'The one I kiss, that's the one — grab him.' He went straight up to Jesus, said, 'How are you, Rabbi?' and kissed him. Jesus said, 'Friend, why this charade?' Then they grabbed Jesus and roughed him up. One of the guys with Jesus pulled out his sword and took a swing at the high priest's servant, cutting off his ear. Jesus said, 'Put your sword back where it belongs. Everyone who uses swords gets destroyed by swords. Don't you realize I could call out to my Father right now and he'd send twelve companies of battle-ready angels — more if I wanted? But if I did that, how would the Scriptures come true that say this is the way it has to happen?' Then Jesus turned to the mob: 'What's with the swords and clubs, like I'm some dangerous criminal? Day after day I've been sitting in the Temple teaching, and you never lifted a finger against me. But this is how it's going down, to make the prophetic writings come true.' Then all the disciples cut and ran.

They took Jesus to the high priest, Caiaphas, for a sham trial. They brought in a bunch of liars to testify against him, but their stories were all over the place. Finally, two came forward and said, 'This fellow said, 'I am able to destroy the temple of God and rebuild it in three days.'' The high priest stood up and asked Jesus, 'Have you no answer?' But Jesus stayed silent. So the high priest said, 'I charge you under oath by the living God: Tell us if you are the Messiah, the Son of God.' Jesus replied, 'You have said so. But I say to all of you: From now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the Mighty One and coming on the clouds of heaven.' The high priest lost it, tore his clothes, and yelled, 'Blasphemy!' The whole council condemned him to death. Then they started spitting in his face and knocking him around, jeering as they slapped him: 'Prophesy, Messiah! Who hit you that time?' All this time, Peter had followed at a safe distance to the high priest's courtyard, slipped in, and blended with the servants to watch how it would all turn out.

Meanwhile, Peter was outside in the courtyard, and a servant girl came up to him and said, 'You also were with Jesus of Galilee.' But he denied it, saying, 'I don't know what you're talking about.' He went out to the gateway, where someone else spotted him and told the people there, 'This fellow was with Jesus of Nazareth.' He denied it again, with an oath: 'I don't know the man!' A little later, the bystanders said to Peter, 'Surely you are one of them; your accent gives you away.' Then he began to call down curses, and he swore to them, 'I don't know the man!' Immediately a rooster crowed, and Peter remembered what Jesus had said: 'Before the rooster crows, you will disown me three times.' And he went outside and wept bitterly.

title: The King They Crucified
paragraphs: As soon as the sun was up, the religious leaders put the final touches on their shady plan to execute Jesus. They tied him up and hauled him off to the governor, Pilate, like a criminal.

When Judas, the friend who betrayed him, realized Jesus was actually going to be killed, he totally lost it. Overcome with guilt, he tried to give the thirty silver coins back to the high priests. 'I sinned! I betrayed an innocent man!' he cried. They shot back, 'What do we care? That's your problem.' Judas threw the money into the Temple, ran out, and hung himself. The high priests picked up the silver pieces but didn't know what to do with them — 'We can't put this blood money, a payment for murder, into the Temple offering.' So they used it to buy the 'Potter's Field' as a burial ground for the homeless. That's how it got the name 'Murder Meadow,' and the name stuck to this day. And just like that, Jeremiah's words came true: they took the thirty silver pieces — the price set on him by the people of Israel — and bought the potter's field, following God's instructions to the letter without even realizing it.

Jesus stood before Governor Pilate, who asked him, 'Are you the King of the Jews?' Jesus replied with a quiet confidence, 'You said it.' But when the priests and elders started piling on the accusations, Jesus didn't say a word. Pilate was baffled. 'Don't you hear all this stuff they're accusing you of?' he asked. Still, Jesus remained silent. The governor was seriously impressed.

It was a custom to release one prisoner chosen by the crowd during the Passover festival. They had a famous bad guy named Barabbas in jail. Pilate, knowing the religious leaders were just jealous, asked the crowd, 'Who should I release? Barabbas, or Jesus, the so-called Christ?' Right in the middle of this, while court was still in session, Pilate's wife sent him a message: 'Don't get mixed up in judging this noble man. I just went through a long, troubled night because of a dream about him.' But the high priests and religious leaders had already talked the crowd into demanding the pardon of Barabbas and the execution of Jesus. 'What should I do with Jesus, the so-called Christ?' Pilate asked. They all shouted, 'Nail him to a cross!' Pilate pushed back, 'But for what crime?' But they just yelled all the louder, 'Nail him to a cross!'

Pilate saw a riot was about to pop off and that he was getting nowhere. He washed his hands in front of everyone and dropped a bomb: 'I'm innocent of this man's blood. This is on you.' The crowd went nuts, shouting, 'We'll take the blame! Us and our kids!' So Pilate freed Barabbas, had Jesus brutally whipped, and handed him over to be crucified.

The governor's soldiers took Jesus into the palace and the whole squad gathered to make fun of him. They stripped him and put a scarlet robe on him, twisted a crown of thorns for his head, and put a staff in his hand like a fake scepter. They knelt down, mocking him, 'Hey, hail King of the Jews!' Then they spit on him and beat him on the head with the staff. When they were done, they put his own clothes back on and led him away to be killed.

On the way out, they forced a random guy from Cyrene, Simon, to carry Jesus' heavy cross. They got to Golgotha, which means 'Skull Hill.' They offered Jesus wine mixed with a painkiller, but after tasting it, he refused. They nailed him to the cross, and then gambled for his clothes. Above his head, they posted the charge: THIS IS JESUS, THE KING OF THE JEWS. They crucified two criminals with him, one on his right and one on his left.

People walking by hurled insults, shaking their heads. 'You were gonna destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days, right? So save yourself! If you're the Son of God, get down from that cross!' The religious leaders joined in the trash talk: 'He saved others, but he can't save himself! King of Israel, huh? Let's see him come down from the cross, and then we'll believe! He trusted God? Let God rescue him now if he wants him!' Even the two criminals crucified next to him dissed him.

From noon until three in the afternoon, the whole land went dark. Around three, Jesus cried out in agony, 'Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?' which means, 'My God, my God, why have you abandoned me?' Some of the bystanders who heard him said, 'He's calling for Elijah.' One of them ran and soaked a sponge in sour wine, lifted it up on a stick so he could drink. The others joked, 'Don't be in such a hurry — let's see if Elijah comes and saves him.' Then Jesus cried out loudly one more time and breathed his last. At that moment, the massive Temple curtain ripped in two from top to bottom. The earth shook, rocks split, and tombs opened. What's more, many bodies of believers asleep in their graves were raised — after Jesus' resurrection, they left the tombs, entered the holy city, and appeared to many people. The Roman captain and his soldiers who were guarding Jesus were terrified by the earthquake and everything happening. They said, 'Seriously, this man was the Son of God.'

Quite a few women were watching from a distance — women who had followed Jesus all the way from Galilee to take care of Him. Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of James and John, Zebedee's sons.

That evening, a rich guy named Joseph from Arimathea showed up. He was a follower of Jesus too. He went to Pilate and asked for Jesus' body, and Pilate gave the green light. Joseph took the body, wrapped it in fresh, clean linen, and laid it in his own brand-new tomb that had been carved out of rock. Then he rolled a massive stone in front of the entrance and left. Mary Magdalene and the other Mary just sat there across from the tomb, watching.

The next day (the day after Preparation Day), the chief priests and Pharisees went to Pilate. 'Sir,' they said, 'we remember that liar said while he was still alive, ‘After three days I will rise again.’ So order the tomb to be locked down tight until day three. Otherwise his disciples might sneak in, steal the body, and tell everyone he rose from the dead. That last lie would be even worse than the first.' Pilate said, 'Take some guards. Go secure it the best you know how.' So they went, sealed the stone, and posted the guards.

title: He's Back. And It's Everything.
paragraphs: After the Sabbath, at the crack of dawn on Sunday, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary went to pay their respects at Jesus' tomb. Out of nowhere, the ground started shaking like crazy. A legit angel of God came down from heaven, rolled away the massive stone like it was nothing, and then just sat on it, chilling. The angel was blazing with light, like lightning, and his clothes were whiter than fresh snow. The guards hired to protect the tomb were so freaked out they literally couldn't move. They were basically frozen in fear.

The angel looked at the women and said, "Don't be scared. I know you're looking for Jesus, the one who was crucified. But he's not here. He has risen, just like he said he would. Come on, check out the spot where he was laid." The women peeked inside, and sure enough, the tomb was empty. The angel then gave them their mission: "Now, go quick and tell his disciples that he's risen from the dead and is on his way to Galilee. You'll see him there. That's the message."

The women were a mix of terrified and totally ecstatic. They took off running from the tomb to find the disciples and tell them the insane news. Suddenly, Jesus himself was right there in front of them. "Good morning!" he said. They dropped to their knees, grabbed his feet, and just started worshiping. Jesus told them, "You're holding on to me for dear life! Don't be afraid. Go tell my brothers to head to Galilee. I'll meet them there."

Meanwhile, some of the guards who had fled the scene went into the city and spilled the beans to the high priests about everything that had just gone down. The religious leaders called an emergency meeting and came up with a seriously shady plan. They paid the soldiers a huge amount of money to spread a lie: "Tell everyone his disciples came in the middle of the night and stole his body while we were asleep." They even promised the soldiers they'd have their backs if the governor found out they were sleeping on the job. The soldiers took the cash and did what they were told. And that fake news story is still floating around today.

The eleven disciples booked it to Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had told them to meet him. When they saw him, they worshiped him, but some of them were still a little hesitant, not fully sure if they could handle this level of commitment. But Jesus didn't let their doubts slow him down. He came to them and dropped this bombshell:

"God has given me all authority in heaven and on earth. So go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and teaching them to obey everything I have commanded you. And for sure, I am with you always, to the very end of the age."
